metadata.name: tessera
metadata.description: Tessera: x402 escrow with an on-chain credit score that sets settlement speed

docs: Tessera: escrow for x402 payments, where an on-chain credit score decides
how long the money is held.
* Funding arrives as a plain SPL `TransferChecked` into ATA(mint, order).
That is exactly what the x402 `exact` scheme on Solana emits, so the
order account can be quoted as `payTo` and no custom scheme is needed.
The program never takes anyone's word that payment happened:
`confirm_funded` reads the vault balance.
* Each order snapshots both parties' tiers. The hold before the merchant
can take the money is the longer of the two tiers' holds. A wallet
nobody knows waits; two wallets with proven history settle at once.
* The score only moves on orders that actually settled, weighted by who
the counterparty was, capped per counterparty, and gated by time.

instructions.name: cancel_unpaid
docs: Abandon an order that was never confirmed as paid. Either party may,
any time; the rent payer may once the payment window has passed.
Anything that reached the vault goes back to the buyer and the vault's
rent to the payer.
The order account itself stays, marked Cancelled, until `close_order`
after the payment window. Closing it at once would let the merchant
reopen the same id -- the same vault address -- for another buyer,
while a payment the real buyer signed for the old order is still in
flight. Anyone may run this again on a Cancelled order whose vault was
recreated and paid into; that money goes to the buyer too.

accounts.name: buyer_token
docs: Only needed if something reached the vault.

instructions.name: close_order
docs: Return a settled order's rent once its review window has passed. This
is also where an instant order nobody objected to stops counting
against the merchant's limit. One the buyer complained about never
does: its rent comes back after the complaint period, but the amount
stays locked for the life of the identity, so an exit scam cannot be
repeated by waiting. A cancelled order closes once its payment window
has passed.

instructions.name: confirm_funded
docs: Permissionless on purpose: the only input it trusts is the vault balance.

instructions.name: deliver
docs: Merchant asserts delivery and commits to what was delivered. The hold
starts now. An order whose tiers call for no hold settles instantly
only while the merchant is inside its instant limit; past it, the
order waits like an Established one.
The limit counts every instant order the buyer has not accepted yet,
so the most a merchant can take and run with is what it already paid
in fees, plus a small base.

instructions.name: ensure_agent
docs: Create a blank credit file for any wallet. Anyone may pay for it: a
buyer agent holding only USDC still gets a profile. The clock on a
blank profile is harmless, because Tenure only counts active periods.

accounts.name: program
docs: Only the program's upgrade authority may create the singleton, so the
first caller after a deployment cannot take it.

instructions.name: open_dispute
docs: The buyer contests a delivery while the hold is still running. An
order that settled instantly has no hold and so cannot be disputed.

instructions.name: open_order
docs: Open an escrow and price its risk. The merchant signs: an order in its
name that it never quoted could otherwise be funded and left to expire,
and the missed delivery would cost it score. The buyer does not sign:
a merchant agent opens the order when it quotes a 402, so the buyer
needs no SOL. A buyer's client must read this account back and check
every field before paying.
`min_hold_secs` lets a buyer ask for more protection than the tiers
call for. It can lengthen the hold, never shorten it.

accounts.name: vault
docs: The escrow vault. Its owner, the order account, is what gets quoted as
the x402 `payTo`, so a buyer can derive and check it from the order id.

accounts.name: merchant
docs: The merchant agrees to every order opened in its name.

instructions.name: refresh_agent
docs: Permissionless: bring a cached score up to date (tenure grows and
penalties decay with time alone).

instructions.name: refund
docs: Give the buyer everything back. The merchant may do it any time before
release. Anyone may do it once the merchant has missed the delivery
deadline, and that costs the merchant score, whoever sends it.

instructions.name: release
docs: Pay the merchant. Anyone may crank this once the hold has elapsed; the
buyer may do it earlier to confirm receipt.

instructions.name: resolve_dispute
docs: The arbiter recorded when the order was opened splits the vault.
Whoever gets less than half lost, and losing costs score.
An arbiter that never answers must not lock the money forever: once
the complaint period has passed since the hold would have ended,
anyone may split the vault evenly. An even split penalises nobody.

instructions.name: set_profile
docs: The wallet names itself and points at its A2A agent card.

instructions.name: submit_review
docs: Either party rates the other, once per order. The review is stored
on-chain in full. Its weight is the volume that settled, scaled by the
reviewer's own tier and capped per pair; a refund weighs nothing.

accounts.name: subject
docs: other party to this order before any score moves.

instructions.name: update_config
docs: Orders already open keep the fee, arbiter and hold they were opened with.

types.name: Agent
docs: One wallet's identity and credit file. Role-agnostic: the same account
tracks behaviour as a buyer and as a merchant.

fields.name: kind
docs: Self-declared: 0 unset, 1 human, 2 AI agent.

fields.name: uri
docs: Where the A2A agent card lives.

fields.name: credit
docs: Settled volume, weighted by counterparty tier and capped per pair.

fields.name: counterparty_points
docs: Sum over counterparties of the best tier weight seen (x100).

fields.name: active_periods
docs: Distinct periods with at least one settled order.

fields.name: fees_paid
docs: Protocol fees paid on this wallet's sales. Sunk cost: this is what
bounds instant settlement.

fields.name: penalty_period
docs: Period in which `penalty_bps` was last brought up to date.

fields.name: rating_sum
docs: Sum of weight x rating.

fields.name: instant_exposure
docs: Instant-settled volume that buyers have not accepted yet. It can never
exceed `score::instant_limit`, which is what bounds an exit scam.

fields.name: arbiter
docs: Resolves disputes. Snapshotted per order, so changing it cannot reach
disputes that are already open.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Wallet whose token account receives protocol fees.

fields.name: mint
docs: The one settlement mint (classic SPL token).

types.name: Order
docs: One escrow. The order account is also the vault's authority, and the
vault is simply ATA(mint, order) -- a legal x402 `payTo`.

fields.name: payer
docs: Paid the rent; gets it back.

fields.name: pair_trusted
docs: Buyer had enough undisputed history with this merchant.

fields.name: hold_secs
docs: Hold the tiers called for at open.

fields.name: instant
docs: Set at delivery if the order settled without a hold.

fields.name: seasoned
docs: An instant order stops counting against the merchant's limit once the
buyer accepts it (3 stars or more) or its review window passes.

fields.name: complained
docs: The buyer rated an instant order 1 or 2 stars.

fields.name: request_hash
docs: Hash of what was ordered (the A2A task or the x402 resource).

fields.name: delivery_hash
docs: Hash of what was delivered.

types.name: Pair
docs: History between one buyer and one merchant. This is the on-chain version
of a card network's "historical footprint": prior undisputed purchases are
evidence that the next one is legitimate.

fields.name: credit_to_buyer
docs: Credit this pair has granted to each side, so the cap is per side.

fields.name: points_to_buyer
docs: Best tier weight (x100) each side has earned from this relationship.

fields.name: rated_by_buyer
docs: Review weight each side has already spent on the other.

types.name: Params
docs: Every tunable lives on-chain so anyone can read the rules a score was
computed under. Devnet runs with compressed time and amounts (see
docs/SCORING.md); the formula is identical on every cluster.

fields.name: period_secs
docs: Length of one activity period in seconds (mainnet target: one day).

fields.name: hold_secs
docs: Settlement hold per tier: New, Building, Established, Trusted.

fields.name: tier_score
docs: Minimum score for tiers 1..=3.

fields.name: tier_periods
docs: Minimum active periods for tiers 1..=3. Time cannot be bought in a burst.

fields.name: credit_full
docs: Credit at which the History component saturates.

fields.name: pair_cap
docs: Most volume from one counterparty that can ever earn credit.

fields.name: tenure_full
docs: Effective periods at which the Tenure component saturates.

fields.name: diversity_full
docs: Counterparty points (x100) at which the Diversity component saturates.

fields.name: review_prior
docs: Weight of the Bayesian prior (3 stars) behind every rating.

fields.name: min_order
docs: Smallest order the program accepts.

fields.name: deliver_secs
docs: Merchant must deliver within this many seconds of funding.

fields.name: unpaid_secs
docs: The rent payer may cancel an unpaid order after this many seconds.

fields.name: review_secs
docs: Reviews are accepted for this long after settlement.

fields.name: complaint_secs
docs: An instant order the buyer rated 1 or 2 stars keeps its amount locked
against the merchant's instant limit for this long.

fields.name: instant_base
docs: Instant exposure every Trusted merchant may carry.

fields.name: instant_fee_pct
docs: Extra instant exposure as a percentage of protocol fees the merchant has paid.

fields.name: pair_history_min
docs: Prior undisputed settled orders that waive the buyer-side hold.

fields.name: pair_age_secs
docs: ...the first of which must be at least this old.

fields.name: penalty_dispute_bps
docs: Penalty (bps of score) for losing a dispute.

fields.name: penalty_expired_bps
docs: Penalty (bps of score) for failing to deliver before the deadline.

fields.name: penalty_decay_bps
docs: Penalty forgiven per period of clean behaviour.

fields.name: weight
docs: What this review counted for: settled volume x reviewer tier weight,
capped per pair. A refunded order weighs 0.

fields.name: orders
docs: Orders released to the merchant.

fields.name: volume
docs: Volume released to the merchant (gross of fee).

fields.name: disputes
docs: Disputes opened (buyer role) or received (merchant role).

fields.name: expired
docs: Merchant role only: orders never delivered before the deadline.

fields.name: instant
docs: Orders that settled instantly.
